source.title: AG-SGD: Angle-Based Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Chong-Ya Song; Alexander P. Pons; Yen K. Kang

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out error across optimizers, including adaptive methods and SGD baselines, but does not test the original studies’ broader tuning conditions.
record.gate_note: Reports optimizer comparison outcomes on MNIST and NSL-KDD. The cited optimizer-comparison findings in the introduction and references are prior work, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out MNIST error comparisons between adaptive optimizers and vanilla or momentum SGD. These bear on V4 under the selected recipe, although comparable learning-rate tuning and matched training performance are not documented.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors attribute AG-SGD's reported cost and error improvements to calibrating past gradients using their angle with current gradients. They acknowledge slower early convergence than AdaMax and report that an alternative nonlinear function can accelerate convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a proposed angle-based optimizer with established optimizers under the paper’s selected settings; the text does not state that learning rates and decay schedules were tuned comparably across methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and batch size differ between experiments; on MNIST the paper reports optimizer-specific convergence behavior over epochs. It also tests AG-SGD parameter settings, but those are not the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: AG-SGD is reported to achieve lower MNIST test error than the compared optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed angle-based optimizer improves held-out performance under this MNIST recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: On NSL-KDD logistic regression, AdaGrad has 24.34% average error versus AG-SGD's 13.71%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AG-SGD outperforms AdaGrad for the tested intrusion-detection classifier.

record.problems: Exact test error rates for the MNIST optimizer comparisons are not stated in the supplied text; the figures and tables are referenced but their detailed values are absent. The study compares selected settings and does not report matched training performance or broad hyperparameter tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Exact optimizer-by-optimizer error values referenced in Tables 3 and 8 are unavailable in the supplied text, so only explicitly stated comparisons and values are recorded.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and the natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Comparable learning-rate and schedule tuning; matched training performance; broader tuning that removes or reverses differences; language benchmarks; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, underfitting, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Memorization-based example removal and random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Its selected-best-run reporting and unspecified comparator tuning restrict interpretation to the reported recipe. The supplied text contains table and figure captions without their numerical contents; those unavailable values are already declared in rows_left_out. No evidence warrants a challenges verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization were not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
The study does not report matched training performance, broader hyperparameter tuning, language benchmarks, weight-decay comparisons, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Dropout was expressly not used; its effect was not tested.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.size_stated: Fully connected Vanilla neural network: 784, 256, 112, and 10 neurons; four layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer test error over 50 epochs; reported as averages of the best 5 results on the same epoch.
rows.baseline: Other optimizers; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.value: Outperformed by all other optimizers with relative significant magnitudes in error reduction; oscillated curves.
rows.note: No exact Adam error-rate value is stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: Adam has higher reported test error than vanilla and momentum SGD. The subject is an optimizer, not a model. Results summarize five selected best runs rather than an unselected run average; the selection protocol and learning-rate settings are insufficiently specified.

rows.size_stated: Fully connected Vanilla neural network: 784, 256, 112, and 10 neurons; four layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer test error over 50 epochs; reported as averages of the best 5 results on the same epoch.
rows.baseline: Other optimizers; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.value: Outperformed by all other optimizers with relative significant magnitudes in error reduction; oscillated curves.
rows.note: The paper additionally calls Nadam the worst performing optimizer, citing increasing cost beyond epoch 40 and non-convergence.
rows.check: Nadam has higher reported test error than vanilla and momentum SGD. Its increasing cost after epoch 40 is a separate convergence observation. The subject is an optimizer; results summarize five selected best runs.

rows.subject: AdaMax
rows.size_stated: Fully connected Vanilla neural network: 784, 256, 112, and 10 neurons; four layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer test error over 50 epochs; reported as averages of the best 5 results on the same epoch.
rows.baseline: Other optimizers; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.value: Performs better in cost/error-rate reduction and stability than Adam and Nadam; converges faster than the remaining optimizers in the first 14 epochs.
rows.note: AdaMax is grouped in the paper’s level-2; its exact error-rate value is not stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: The relevant baseline is vanilla or momentum SGD, not Adam or Nadam. The stated performance hierarchy places AdaMax below those SGD methods in test-error reduction, supporting the V4 direction. Faster early convergence does not establish better final generalization. The subject is an optimizer.

rows.check: The reported 24.34% versus 13.71% error comparison concerns intrusion-detection logistic regression and AG-SGD, outside V4's image/language benchmarks and standard SGD comparator. It cannot challenge V4. The subject is an optimizer.

relationships.condition: Adam and Nadam on MNIST with the sigmoid fully connected classifier, batch size 8, and 50 epochs
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 explicitly report worse test-error reduction than all other optimizers, including vanilla and momentum SGD in R6 and R7, under the paper's selected settings.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test-error reduction was worse for Adam and Nadam than vanilla and momentum SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: AdaMax, AMSGrad, and RMSprop on the same MNIST recipe
relationships.reason: The text places R3–R5 below the vanilla/momentum SGD group in R6–R7 on test-error reduction, although exact differences are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test-error reduction favored vanilla and momentum SGD over AdaMax, AMSGrad, and RMSprop, but exact differences were unavailable and the comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: AdaDelta and AdaGrad on the same MNIST recipe
relationships.reason: R8 and R9 share the better conventional-optimizer group with vanilla and momentum SGD; the reported disadvantage therefore depends on which adaptive optimizer is used.
relationships.display_finding: AdaDelta, AdaGrad, vanilla SGD, and momentum SGD were reportedly among the better-performing optimizers, but this result remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Adam and Nadam on the MNIST fully connected classifier
reader_labels.reason: Both adaptive methods are stated to be outperformed by all other optimizers in error reduction (R1, R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Adaptive methods on MNIST, including AdaMax, AMSGrad, and RMSprop
reader_labels.reason: These adaptive methods are reported as outperforming Adam and Nadam, and AdaDelta and AdaGrad are among the lowest-error optimizers (R3, R4, R5, R8, R9).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: AdaDelta and AdaGrad on MNIST; AdaGrad on NSL-KDD
reader_labels.reason: These adaptive methods are reported among the lowest-error MNIST optimizers, and AdaGrad has 24.34% error versus AG-SGD’s 13.71% on NSL-KDD, with no evidence here that adaptive methods uniformly fare worse (R8, R9, R11).
